elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted Article XXI-A opens "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall ...", so all three limbs (a)-(c) attach to both expiry and termination.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "at Licensee's request, provide transition assistance for up to six (6) months". The request condition is not tied only to anticipated expiry; it operates after any expiry or termination.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty (30) days, return to Licensee all data submitted by or on behalf of Licensee or generated for Licensee through use of the Licensed Technology (\"Licensee Data\")", running from the expiry/termination anchor in the lead-in.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return "in a standard machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "after such return, delete all Licensee Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing" — deletion and certification expressly sequenced after return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same lead-in language "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Six months of assistance exceeds the 90-day fallback minimum; this is the preferred threshold, not an unnecessary excess over a fallback cap.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return of all Licensee Data within thirty (30) days of expiry/termination in machine-readable format.

reasons: All six preferred elements are met by the single inserted Article XXI-A; the fallback is also satisfied a fortiori.
The insertion is a concise new clause for a genuinely missing provision: no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no extra remedies, procedures or damages categories beyond the checklist limbs.

Because the document contains no "Customer Data"/"Licensee Data" concept, the short parenthetical definition of "Licensee Data" is necessary to make limbs (b) and (c) operable rather than an extra, and it avoids a dangling undefined term.

Existing Article XXI is left untouched: Licensee's five-day return of Licensed Technology, the officer certification, and Licensor's survival sentence all survive. The new clause covers Licensee's own data only, so there is no contradiction with the retained one-way return obligation.
No new assignment exception, licence, or unrelated obligation is introduced; timing, remedies and commercial mechanics elsewhere are unaffected.
